Tischler and Piet Maes The citation for this ICTV Report chapter is the summary published as: Bradfute, S. B., Calisher, C. H., Klempa, B., Klingström, J., Kuhn, J. H., Laenen, L., Tischler, N. D., & Maes, P. (2024). ICTV Virus Taxonomy Profile: Hantaviridae 2024, Journal of General Virology 105, 001975 Corresponding author: Piet Maes ( [email protected] ) Edited by: Holly Hughes and Evelien Adriaenssens Posted: March 2024, updated June 2024 Summary Hantaviridae is a family for negative-sense RNA viruses with genomes of about 10.5–14.6 kb (Table 1 Hantaviridae ). The family includes eight genera ( Actinovirus and Percilovirus (subfamily Actantavirinae ), Agnathovirus (subfamily Agantavirinae ), Loanvirus , Mobatvirus , Orthohantavirus and Thottimvirus (subfamily Mammantavirinae ), and Reptillovirus (subfamily Repantavirinae ). These viruses are maintained in and/or transmitted by small mammals, but also by fish and reptiles. Several orthohantaviruses can infect humans, causing mild, severe, and sometimes-fatal diseases. Hantavirids produce enveloped virions containing three single-stranded RNA segments with open reading frames (ORFs) that encode a nucleoprotein (N), a glycoprotein precursor (GPC), and large (L) protein containing an RNA-directed RNA polymerase (RdRP) domain. Table 1 Hantaviridae. Characteristics of members of the family Hantaviridae. Characteristic Description* Example Hantaan virus (S segment: M14626; M segment: M14627; L segment: X55901), species Orthohantavirus hantanense Virion Enveloped, pleomorphic virions 80–160 nm in diameter with heterodimeric surface spikes Genome Three single-stranded RNA molecules (segments): small (S; 1.0–3.0 kb), medium (M; 3.4–4.8 kb), and large (L; 5.3–6.8 kb) Replication Ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes containing anti-genomic RNA serve as coding templates for synthesis of genomic RNA Translation Proteins are produced from capped and non-polyadenylated mRNAs. The 5′-cap structure is obtained via cap-snatching from cellular mRNAs Host range Fish (actinoviruses, agnathoviruses, perciloviruses), mammals (orthohantaviruses), and reptiles (reptilloviruses) Taxonomy Realm Riboviria , kingdom Orthornavirae , phylum Negarnaviricota , class Bunyaviricetes , order Elliovirales ; the family includes four subfamilies, eight genera, and 55 species * mostly based on experiments with mammalian orthohantaviruses Viruses assigned to each of the seven genera form genus-specifc monophyletic clades based on phylogenetic analysis of concatenated L protein/RdRP, glycoprotein and N sequences. Viruses from all seven genera share one or more of the following characteristics: (i) enveloped pleomorphic virions; (ii) tri-segmented, negative-sense RNA genome without polyadenylated tracts at the 3′-end; (iii) genomic sequence complementarity at the 5′- and 3′-ends; and (iv) capped but not polyadenylated virus mRNAs ( Maes et al., 2004 ). Piscine Hosts Genus Actinovirus . Viruses in this genus infect actinopterygian (percid, ogcocephalid, and triacanthodid, and possibly goblid and melanotaeniid) fish. Genus Agnathovirus . Viruses in this genus infect agnathan (myxinid) fish. Genus Percilovirus . Viruses in this genus infect actinopterygian ( gobiid, lophiid ) fish. Mammalian Hosts Genus Loanvirus. Viruses in this genus infect rhinolophid, verspertillionid, and possibly nycterid bats and possibly murid rodents. Genus Mobatvirus. Viruses in this genus infect emballonurid, hipposiderid, pteropodid and possibly molossid, and vespertillionid bats and soricid and talpid eulipotyphla. Genus Orthohantavirus. Viruses assigned to this genus infect soricid and talpid eulipotyphla and muroid and possibly dipodoid rodents. Genus Thottimvirus. Viruses in this genus infect soricid and possibly talpid eulipotyphla. Reptilian Hosts Genus Reptillovirus . Viruses in this genus infect gekkonid and possibly scincid reptiles. Virion Morphology Only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Physicochemical and physical properties Only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Nucleic acid Hantavirids have tri-segmented, negative-sense RNA genomes (S, M, and L segments). The viral mRNAs are not polyadenylated and contain a 5′-methylated cap and several non-templated nucleotides at the 5′-end that are derived from host cell mRNAs via cap snatching ( Schmaljohn et al., 1985 , Jonsson and Schmaljohn 2001 , Vaheri et al., 2013 ). Further information is only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Proteins Hantavirids typically express three structural proteins. The most abundant structural protein in a hantavirion is N, which encapsidates the hantaviral genomic segments. The least abundant protein is L, which mediates viral genome replication and transcription. Two glycoprotein subunits, G N and G C , are produced from GPC and mediate entry of hantavirions ( Schmaljohn et al., 1985 , Spiropoulou 2001 , Vaheri et al., 2013 ). Specifics are only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Lipids Not reported but are likely derived from the Golgi apparatus and/or the host cell plasma membrane and therefore likely composed of phospholipids, glycolipids, fatty acids, and sterols. Carbohydrates Only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Genome organization and replication S RNA encodes N and in some viruses NSs ( Jääskeläinen et al., 2007 , Vera-Otarola et al., 2012 ), M RNA encodes GPC, and the L RNA encodes L with its RdRP, helicase, and endonuclease domains ( Jonsson and Schmaljohn 2001 ) (Figure 1 Hantaviridae ). Specifics are only known for members of the genus Orthohantavirus (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Figure 1 Hantaviridae . Genome organization of representative hantaviruses. The 5′- and 3′- ends of all segments are complementary at their termini, likely promoting the formation of panhandle RNP complexes within the virion . GPC , glycoprotein precursor gene; L , large (protein) gene; N , nucleoprotein gene. Biology Hantavirids have been found in actinopterygian (gobiid, lophiid, percid, ogcocephalid, and triacanthodid, and possibly goblid and melanotaeniid) and agnathan (myxinid) fish; in emballonurid, hipposiderid, pteropodid, rhinolophid, verspertillionid, and possibly molossid and nycterid bats; in soricid and talpid eulipotyphla; in muroid and possibly dipodoid rodents; in gekkonid and possibly scincid reptiles; and potentially in coleopteran and plectopteran insects (see genus pages for details). Only orthohantaviruses are known to cause diseases (see Orthohantavirus genus page). Antigenicity Systematic antigenicity studies have only been reported for orthohantaviruses (see Orthohantavirus genus page). species demarcation criteria The availability of at least coding-complete sequences of all three genome segments may be sufficient for hantavirid classification in the absence of a cultured isolate. Demarcation of genera is based upon DivErsity pArtitioning by hieRarchical Clustering (DEmARC) analysis) using concatenated deduced S, M, and L segment expression product sequences ( Hantaviridae: current classification and future perspectives, Viruses, 11, 9, e0788">Laenen et al., 2019 ). DEmARC analysis gave a frequency distribution of Pairwise Evolutionary Distance (PED) values of which the threshold of 0.1 gave an optimal clustering cost of zero and is used as the hantavirid species demarcation criterium. Genera are demarked by a PED-value threshold of 0.95 and subfamilies are demarcated based on their distinct clustering in a Bayesian maximum clade credibility tree and a PED-value threshold of 3.5. Relationships within the family Phylogenetic relationships across the family have been estimated using Bayesian maximum clade credibility trees generated from complete N, GPC, and L amino-acid sequences; similar topologies are obtained with concatenated N and GPC sequences (Figure 2 Hantaviridae ). Figure 2 Hantaviridae . Maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree inferred using IQ-TREE. The tree was constructed based on 53 concatenated S and M segment (amino acid) sequences using the LG+R9 model of sequence evolution. Branch lengths represent the estimated number of substitutions per site. Bootstrap support values (>70%) are indicated at nodes, reflecting the degree of confidence in the branching pattern. Relationships with other taxa Hantavirids are closely related to bunyaviral crulivirids, fimovirids, peribunyavirids, phasmavirids, tulasvirids, and tospovirids ( Wolf et al., 2018 , Herath et al., 2020 ). Using the Master Species List Using the Virus Metadata Resource Using the Find the Species tool Using the ICTV Report Webinar Webinar on Virus Taxonomy Webinar on Finding Information GitHub Repository Zenodo Repository Email ICTV Help ‏‏‎ ‎ ICTV Report Book: Hantaviridae Family: Hantaviridae Subfamily: Actantavirinae Genus: Actinovirus Genus: Percilovirus Subfamily: Agantavirinae Genus: Agnathovirus Subfamily: Mammantavirinae Genus: Loanvirus Genus: Mobatvirus Genus: Orthohantavirus Genus: Thottimvirus Subfamily: Repantavirinae Genus: Reptillovirus Authors: Hantaviridae Citation: Hantaviridae References: Hantaviridae Resources: Hantaviridae Species List: Hantaviridae Subfamily: Mammantavirinae Genus: Orthohantavirus Distinguishing features Sixty different viruses are classified in the genus Orthohantavius. These viruses typically infect specific soricid and talpid eulipotyphla and muroid and possibly dipodoid rodents. Orthohantaviruses are the only hantavirids known to cause disease in humans ( Schmaljohn and Hjelle 1997 , Jonsson et al., 2010 , Kuhn and Schmaljohn 2023 , Vial et al., 2023 ). Virion Morphology Orthohantavirions are pleomorphic in shape, mostly spherical of 80–160 nm in diameter ( Huiskonen et al., 2010 ), and surrounded by a membrane envelope that is decorated with glycoprotein (GP) spikes composed of G N and G C subunits (Figure 1 Orthohantavirus ). The virion envelope is 5 nm thick and is decorated with square shaped spikes, consisting of tetrameric G N -G C heterodimers, which protrude 10 nM from the membrane forming a surface lattice of local symmetry interrupted by empty membrane spots ( Hung et al., 1983 , Huiskonen et al., 2010 , Battisti et al., 2011 , Parvate et al., 2019 , Serris et al., 2020 , Guardado-Calvo and Rey 2021 ). Isolated ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes are composed of individual segment genomic RNA encapsidated by nucleoprotein (N) ( Tao et al., 1987 , Huiskonen et al., 2010 , Battisti et al., 2011 , Hepojoki et al., 2012 , Guo et al., 2016 , Arragain et al., 2019 ). Virions assemble and bud from the Golgi complex or cell surface membranes, depending on the virus ( Goldsmith et al., 1995 , Parvate et al., 2019 ). Figure 1 Orthohantavirus. A, B) Electron micrographs of Tula virus particles adapted from ( Huiskonen et al., 2010 ). C) Schematic illustration of an orthohantavirus particle. Shown is a spherical and enveloped (grey) particle with glycoprotein spikes (G N yellow, G C blue) inserted in a bilaminar lipid envelope. The S (small), M (medium), and L (large) RNP (ribonucleoprotein) complexes inside the particle consist of N (nucleoprotein, green) and L (large protein, pink). ViralZone image reproduced courtesy of SwissBioPics. Physicochemical and physical properties Virion buoyant densities in sucrose and CsCl are 1.15–1.18 ( White et al., 1982 ) and 1.20–1.21 g cm −3 , respectively ( Schmaljohn et al., 1983 ). Virions are sensitive to chemical inactivation with, for instance, methanol, paraformaldehyde, acetone/methanol, N -ethylmaleimide or detergents, as well as physical methods such as heat, gamma irradiation or UV irradiation ( Kraus et al., 2005 , Strandin et al., 2011 , Elveborg et al., 2022 ). Nucleic acid Orthohantavirus genomes are linear tri-segmented RNA molecules of negative polarity. The genomes are about 11.1–12.3 kb in length (small [S] segment: 1.2–2.1 kb; medium [M] segment: 3.4–3.8 kb; large [L] segment: 6.5–6.6 kb). Proteins Orthohantaviruses typically express three structural proteins (Table 1 Orthohantavirus ). The most abundant structural protein in an orthohantavirion is N, which encapsidates the orthohantaviral genomic segments. The least abundant protein is L, which mediates viral genome replication and transcription. Two glycoprotein subunits, G N and G C , mediate virion entry. G N and G C and non-structural proteins are encoded as a precursor polyprotein. Table 1 Orthohantavirus . Location and function of orthohantavirus structural proteins. Protein Location, mass, and function Reference Nucleoprotein (N) Structural virion protein (about 48 kD). Oligomerizes and encapsidates orthohantaviral genomic segments and hence component of RNPs. Binds to L and G N ( Mir et al., 2010 , Reuter and Krüger 2018 , Arragain et al., 2019 ) Nonstructural protein (NSs) Non-structural protein encoded by some orhtohantaviruses. Has type I interferon inhibitory activity. May occur as multiple isoforms. ( Vera-Otarola et al., 2020 , Binder et al., 2021 ) Glycoprotein (GP) Structural virion protein consisting of two subunits (G N : about 70-75 kD, G C : about 50-55 kD). Produced via proteolytic cleavage from the genome-encoded precursor GPC. Projects from virion membranes as tetrameric GP spikes composed of G N and G C heterodimers. GP mediates cell- receptor binding; as a class II fusion machine it induces virion-cell membrane fusion and, thereby cell entry. G N binds to N and RNA ( Spiropoulou et al., 2003 , Tischler et al., 2005 , Cifuentes-Muñoz et al., 2014 , Li et al., 2016 , Willensky et al., 2016 , Rissanen et al., 2017 , Zhu et al., 2018 , Bignon et al., 2019 , Sperber et al., 2019 ) Large protein (L) Structural virion protein (246 kD) with RdRP, helicase, and endoribonuclease domains. Component of the RNP inside virions. Binds to N and RNA. Oligomerizes and mediates transcription and replication of viral RNA segments. Mediates cap-snatching for viral mRNA capping. ( Kukkonen et al., 2005 , Cheng et al., 2014 , Rothenberger et al., 2016 , Jeeva et al., 2019 , Durieux Trouilleton et al., 2023 ) Genome organization and replication The orthohantavirus genome consists of three negative-sense RNA molecules, termed S (small), M (medium), and L (large) (Figure 2 Orthohantavirus ). Figure 2 Orthohantavirus. Schematic representation of orthohantavirus genome organization. Orthohantavirus genomic segments assume circular forms via non-covalent binding of complementary and highly conserved 3′- and 5′-terminal sequences. Genomic segment reassortment mostly occurs among viruses belonging to the same species but interspecies reassortment likely occurs occasionally ( Klempa 2018 , Petazzi et al., 2021 ). Orthohantavirus infection starts with virion attachment, mediated by G N and G C , to cell-surface attachment factors and entry via the endosomal route ( Shtanko et al., 2014 ) (Figure 3 Orthohantavirus ). Figure 3 Orthohantavirus . Lifecycle of orthohantaviruses. (1) Virion attachment; (2) virion uptake; (3) virion-cell membrane fusion; (4) transcription; (5) translation; (6) replication; (7) virion assembly; and (8) virion egress. After engaging a cellular receptor, protocadherin 1 in the case of American orthohantaviruses, virion-membrane fusion results in early or late endosomal release, depending on the virus, of the virion RNP complex into the cytoplasm in a pH-dependent manner ( Jangra et al., 2018 , Mittler et al., 2019 , Torriani et al., 2019 , Dieterle et al., 2021 ). During primary transcription L generates uncapped antigenomic RNA molecules that are then capped using host cell-derived capped primers (cap snatching). L and S segment-transcribed mRNAs are translated by free ribosomes ( Garcin et al., 1995 , Jeeva et al., 2019 , Meier et al., 2021 ). M segment-transcribed mRNA is translated by membrane-bound ribosomes, with the expressed GPC which is likely co-translationally cleaved by cellular proteases to yield G N and G C . The synthesis of the antigenome by L protein serves as a template for genomic RNA replication. Secondary transcription amplifies the synthesis of mRNAs and genome replication. During morphogenesis, G N and G C accumulate in the Golgi apparatus, modified host membranes are acquired, and virions bud into the Golgi. Biology Genus Orthohantavirus includes 38 species for 60 distinct viruses. These viruses and their unclassified, potential relatives, subclinically, and often chronically, infect specific soricid and talpid eulipotyphla, and muroid and possibly dipodoid rodents ( Jonsson et al., 2010 , Wu et al., 2018 , Chen et al., 2023 , Kuhn and Schmaljohn 2023 ). Orthohantaviruses are overall distributed worldwide, but the individual geographic distribution is dependent on host range. At least some orthohantaviruses may not be as restricted to a particular host as originally thought, but may be carried by animals of multiple hosts ( Goodfellow et al., 2021 , Quizon et al., 2022 , Gu et al., 2023 ). Orthohantaviruses are the only hantavirids known to cause disease (all in humans) and all disease-causing viruses are rodent-borne. Human infection may occur after inhalation of aerosolized excreta or secreta of infected rodents or direct rodent contact. The two WHO-recognized orthohantavirus-caused diseases are hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), caused by Asian and European viruses (in particular Dobrava virus [DOBV], Hantaan virus [HTNV], Puumala virus [PUUV] and Seoul virus [SEOV]), and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), a frequently lethal disease caused by viruses from the Americas (in particular Andes virus [ANDV] and Sin Nombre virus [SNV]) ( Vial et al., 2023 ). The hamster model of wild-type ANDV infection is lethal and largely mimics human HPS ( Hooper et al., 2001 ). After SNV infection in nonhuman primates, some animals develop an HPS-like disease, but cell passage of SNV can result in mutations that render the virus non-pathogenic in this model ( Safronetz et al., 2014 ). Many rodent models result in a chronic, asymptomatic infection, and these have been used in early-stage therapeutic studies ( Strandin et al., 2020 ). However, recent advances have been made in development of an HFRS mouse model using HTNV variants ( Wei et al., 2022 ). Orthohantavirus animal models are reviewed in ( Golden et al., 2015 ). Antigenicity There is considerable serum cross-reactivity between the nucleocapsids of hantavirids, but neutralizing antibodies targeting Gn/Gc are more specific. SNV was first identified as a hantavirid based on cross-reactivity of patient sera with other orthohantavirus antigens ( 1993 ). Similarly, rodents that carried SNV were identified in serosurveys using non-SNV orthohantavirus antigens, since SNV had not been isolated at the time ( Childs et al., 1994 ). Species demarcation criteria Demarcation of species is based upon DivErsity pArtitioning by hieRarchical Clustering (DEmARC) analysis) using concatenated deduced S, M, and L segment expression product sequences ( Laenen et al., 2019 ). Phylogenetic relationships across the genus have been estimated using maximum likelihood trees generated from complete N, GPC and L amino-acid sequences, and for N and GPC amino-acid sequences (Figure 2 Hantaviridae ). Hantaviridae ~ ViralZone Skip to main content ViralZone Hantaviridae (taxid:1980413) VIRION Enveloped, spherical. Diameter from 80 to 120nm. GENOME Segmented Negative-stranded RNA linear genome, L segment is between 6.8 and 12 kb, M segment between 3.2 and 4.9 kb and S segment between 1 and 3 kb. Encodes for four to six proteins. Some hantaviruses also encode a NSs protein on their S segment. GENE EXPRESSION The viral RNA dependent RNA polymerase (L) binds to a promoter on each encapsidated segment, and transcribes the mRNA. These are capped by L protein during synthesis using cap snatching . Transcription is terminated by a strong hairpin sequence at the end of each gene. Puumala virus expressed an additional NSs by leaky scanning in the NS gene. ENZYMES RNA-dependent RNA polymerase L Cap Snatching endonuclease L REPLICATION CYTOPLASMIC Virus attaches to host receptors though Gn-Gc glycoprotein dimer, and is endocytosed into vesicles in the host cell. Fusion of virus membrane with the vesicle membrane; ribonucleocapsid segments are released in the cytoplasm. Transcription , viral mRNAs are capped in the cytoplasm. Replication presumably starts when enough nucleoprotein is present to encapsidate neo-synthetized antigenomes and genomes. The ribonucleocapsids buds at Golgi apparatus, releasing the virion by exocytosis. The hantaviruses (Hantaviridae) ~ ViralZone Skip to main content ViralZone Back to Andes virus resource There are approximately 92 known viruses in the family Hantaviridae, classified into 52 species. Each species is typically adapted to a specific reservoir host, most commonly rodents, but also bats and moles. With the notable exception of Andes virus, hantaviruses are generally not transmitted from person to person. Based on their geographic distribution, evolutionary relationships, and the diseases they cause in humans, hantaviruses can be broadly divided into three major groups: New World hantaviruses (the Americas) These viruses cause Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS), a severe respiratory disease. Important examples include Sin Nombre virus and Andes virus. Annual incidence are about 100 cases per year (Andes virus) about 25 cases per year (Sin Nombre virus) Old World hantaviruses (Asia) These viruses are responsible for Hantavirus hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), which is characterized by fever, hemorrhage, and acute kidney injury. Major examples include Hantaan virus and Seoul virus. Annual incidence: more than 10,000 cases worldwide Old World hantaviruses (Europe) European hantaviruses typically cause a milder form of HFRS known as Nephropathia epidemica (NE). The main causative agents are Puumala virus and Dobrava-Belgrade virus. Annual incidence: more than 1,000 cases Together, these viruses represent an important and diverse group of zoonotic pathogens that can cause severe disease following accidental transmission from their natural animal hosts to humans.

papers.title: CD8+ regulatory T cells limit immunopathology but impair viral clearance in Hantaan virus infection.
papers.abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8 + T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8 + regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8 + Tregs (CD122 + Eomes + CD49d lo KIR + ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8 + T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8 + Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8 + Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

analysis.background: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Hantaan virus, virus‑specific CD8⁺ T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology.
analysis.methods: The authors characterized an HLA‑E (Qa‑1)‑restricted CD8⁺ regulatory T‑cell subset in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model.
analysis.results: CD8⁺ Tregs (CD122⁺ Eomes⁺ CD49d^lo KIR⁺) were markedly reduced in patients’ blood and displayed a terminally differentiated phenotype (high KLRG‑1, NKG2A, CTLA‑4, Fas‑L) correlating with disease severity; two HTNV glycoprotein nonapeptides binding Qa‑1 were identified; immunization with these peptides protected wild‑type mice from renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock‑in mice cleared virus more efficiently but suffered exacerbated renal damage; Qa‑1‑restricted CD8⁺ Tregs suppressed effector CD8⁺ proliferation via peptide‑specific, CD8/TCR‑dependent TGF‑β secretion; the D227K mutation reshaped Treg phenotype, increasing inhibitory receptors and TGF‑β in bulk cells but impairing antigen‑specific suppressive function.
analysis.contribution: The findings indicate that HLA‑E/Qa‑1‑restricted CD8⁺ Tregs restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection at the cost of delayed viral elimination, highlighting a potential therapeutic axis for HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is provided; detailed sample sizes, statistical analyses, and broader validation are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Hantaan virus, virus‑specific CD8⁺ T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Methods: The authors characterized an HLA‑E (Qa‑1)‑restricted CD8⁺ regulatory T‑cell subset in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. Results: CD8⁺ Tregs were reduced in patients, showed a terminally differentiated phenotype linked to severity, and two Qa‑1‑binding HTNV peptides were identified; immunized wild‑type mice had less renal pathology, while D227K mice cleared virus better but had worse pathology; CD8⁺ Tregs suppressed effector proliferation via peptide‑specific TGF‑β, and the D227K mutation altered Treg phenotype and function. Contribution: The study shows HLA‑E/Qa‑1‑restricted CD8⁺ Tregs limit immunopathology at the expense of delayed clearance, suggesting a therapeutic target for HFRS. Limitations: Only an abstract is available; detailed methods, sample sizes, and statistical data are not reported.

papers.title_zh: CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞限制免疫病理,但削弱 汉滩病毒 感染中的病毒清除。

analysis_zh.background: 在由 汉滩病毒 引起的 肾综合征出血热 中,特异性病毒的 CD8+ T 细胞既介导病毒清除,也导致免疫病理学。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者在肾综合征出血热患者及小鼠 HTNV 感染模型中,对 HLA‐E (Qa‐1) 限制的 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞亚群进行了表征。
analysis_zh.results: 患者血液中的 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞(CD122+ Eomes+ CD49d^lo KIR+)显著减少,并表现出终末分化表型(KLRG‐1、NKG2A、CTLA‐4、Fas‐L 高表达),其程度与疾病严重程度相关;鉴定出两种结合 Qa‐1 的 HTNV 糖蛋白九肽;用这些肽免疫可保护野生型小鼠免于肾脏免疫病理,而 D227K 敲入小鼠虽能更高效清除病毒,却出现加重的肾损伤;Qa‐1 限制的 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞通过肽特异性、CD8/TCR 依赖的 TGF‐β 分泌抑制效应 CD8+ 增殖;D227K 突变重塑了 Treg 表型,提升了整体细胞的抑制受体和 TGF‐β 表达,但削弱了抗原特异性抑制功能。
analysis_zh.contribution: 研究结果表明,HLA‐E/Qa‐1 限制的 CD8+ 调节性 T 细胞在 HTNV 感染期间抑制免疫病理,但以延迟病毒清除为代价,突显了其作为肾综合征出血热及相关病毒性出血热潜在治疗靶点的价值。

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of serological, molecular and rapid tests for human hantavirus disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human hantavirus disease is potentially lethal and overlaps clinically with other febrile, renal, and cardiopulmonary syndromes. Diagnostic performance varies by viral species, specimen type, sampling timing, and reference standard. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and compare the diagnostic accuracy of serologic, molecular, rapid, multiplex, and antigen-detection tests for human hantavirus infection or disease. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261398030). MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through May 20, 2026. Human studies with an eligible index test and verifiable reference standard were included. Diagnostic accuracy data were extracted when possible. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and certainty with GRADE-DTA. Primary meta-analyses used platform-specific univariate logit-scale models; hierarchical bivariate/HSROC sensitivity analyses were performed for eligible strata. RESULTS: Sixty-three studies were included; 24 contributed 2 × 2 data and 22 primary comparisons entered the main synthesis. ELISA/EIA showed sensitivity of 98.0% and specificity of 98.8%, with low certainty. Rapid-format assays showed sensitivity of 97.4% and specificity of 97.2%, also with low certainty. Molecular tests had specificity of 99.5% and sensitivity of 85.6%. Bivariate sensitivity analyses for ELISA/EIA and rapid-format assays produced similar estimates to the primary models. CONCLUSIONS: In the available low-certainty evidence, ELISA/EIA serology is the best-supported platform, but this is not a universal recommendation. Molecular and rapid tests may be useful in specific contexts and require prospective validation.

analysis_zh.background: 人类 汉坦病毒 疾病潜在致死,并在临床上与其他发热、肾脏及心肺综合征相重叠。
analysis_zh.main_directions: 本综述比较血清学、分子、快速、多重及抗原检测方法,指出诊断性能随病毒种类、标本类型、采样时间和参考标准而异。
analysis_zh.current_state: ELISA/EIA 的灵敏度约为 98%,特异度为 98.8%;快速检测试剂的灵敏度和特异度均约为 97%;分子检测的灵敏度约为 85.6%,特异度为 99.5%,但所有估计的确定性均较低。
analysis_zh.gaps: 仅少数研究提供完整的 2×2 数据,偏倚风险中等,总体确定性低,因而无法给出普遍性建议。
analysis_zh.future_research: 需要在 汉坦病毒 物种及临床情境下开展前瞻性、设计严谨的诊断准确性研究,以验证分子和快速平台并提升证据确定性。

papers.summary_zh: 背景：人类 汉坦病毒 疾病潜在致死,并在临床上与其他发热、肾脏及心肺综合征相重叠。 主要方向：本综述比较血清学、分子、快速、多重及抗原检测方法,指出诊断性能随病毒种类、标本类型、采样时间和参考标准而异。 研究现状：ELISA/EIA 的灵敏度约为 98%,特异度为 98.8%;快速检测试剂的灵敏度和特异度均约为 97%;分子检测的灵敏度约为 85.6%,… 不足：仅少数研究提供完整的 2×2 数据,偏倚风险中等,总体确定性低,因而无法给出普遍性建议。 后续研究：需要在 汉坦病毒 物种及临床情境下开展前瞻性、设计严谨的诊断准确性研究,以验证分子和快速平台并提升证据确定性。

papers.title: Dinámica de la Información Digital en español ante un riesgo emergente de salud pública: análisis exploratorio del caso hantavirus
papers.abstract: Este artículo analiza la dinámica temporal de la información digital en español relacionada con el hantavirus como caso de un riesgo emergente de salud pública. Se realizó un estudio observacional, retrospectivo, descriptivo y exploratorio a partir de publicaciones digitales recuperadas mediante un canal de monitoreo orientado a México. De las 1,054 publicaciones en español recuperadas, 899 conformaron el corpus final, correspondiente al periodo del 7 de mayo al 8 de agosto de 2026. La delimitación temporal y la exclusión de registros sin fecha válida definieron esta selección. El volumen de publicaciones se analizó por día y los periodos de mayor actividad se identificaron a partir de la media y la desviación estándar. Se observaron tres episodios principales, con máximos de 78, 139 y 169 publicaciones. Los seis días clasificados como de alta actividad reunieron el 71.5% del corpus. El mayor volumen se registró el 19 de mayo, fecha en la que predominaron los contenidos relacionados con vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica (41.4%). La actividad informativa mostró una clara concentración temporal y una composición distinta entre episodios. Estos patrones permiten caracterizar cómo evolucionó el entorno informativo ante acontecimientos de interés para la salud pública. El volumen de publicaciones, sin embargo, no representa una medida de intensidad epidemiológica.

An observational, retrospective, descriptive, and exploratory study was conducted using digital publications retrieved through a monitoring channel focused on Mexico. Of the 1,054 Spanish-language publications retrieved, 899 comprised the final corpus, covering the period from May 7 to August 8, 2026. This selection was defined by the temporal delimitation and the exclusion of records without a valid publication date. Publication volume was analyzed by day, and periods of higher activity were identified using the mean and standard deviation. Three main episodes were observed, with peaks of 78, 139, and 169 publications. The six days classified as high-activity accounted for 71.5% of the corpus. The highest volume was recorded on May 19, when content related to epidemiological surveillance or investigation predominated (41.4%). Keywords: hantavirus, public health, infodemiology, temporal dynamics, risk communication Artículo recibido 20 agosto 2026 Aceptado para publicación: 20 setiembre 2026 pág. 5865 INTRODUCCIÓN La expansión de los medios digitales ha transformado la producción, difusión y consulta de información relacionada con acontecimientos de salud pública. Durante brotes y emergencias sanitarias, la atención informativa puede cambiar de manera importante a lo largo del tiempo. Casos, alertas, acciones institucionales y medidas de prevención pueden generar variaciones tanto en el volumen como en el contenido de las noticias y otras fuentes digitales (Liu et al., 2020; Kim, 2022; Gozzi et al., 2020; Islam et al., 2023). El análisis de esta información ha dado lugar a enfoques como la epidemiología digital, la infodemiología y la infovigilancia. Estas aproximaciones aprovechan información disponible públicamente en Internet y otras fuentes externas a los sistemas tradicionales de salud para estudiar enfermedades, epidemias y otros fenómenos de interés sanitario (Salathé, 2018; Mavragani, 2020). La actividad registrada en fuentes digitales no constituye un indicador directo de incidencia, prevalencia o severidad epidemiológica. Se ha documentado que la atención en línea puede estar estrechamente relacionada con la cobertura mediática y presentar patrones temporales diferentes a los observados en la evolución epidemiológica (Gozzi et al., 2020; Sousa-Pinto et al., 2020). Por ello, el volumen y contenido de las publicaciones pueden utilizarse para caracterizar la atención informativa y examinar sus variaciones ante diferentes acontecimientos, como complemento para comprender el entorno informativo asociado con situaciones de interés para la salud pública (Berg et al., 2021; Méndiz-Noguero et al., 2023; Barrientos-Gutiérrez et al., 2025). El hantavirus constituye un caso pertinente para este tipo de análisis por tratarse de una zoonosis asociada principalmente con reservorios roedores, capaz de producir enfermedad grave y que continúa representando un desafío para la vigilancia y la respuesta de salud pública (Edegbo et al., 2026; Gupta, 2026). A partir de este contexto, el objetivo del presente estudio fue caracterizar la dinámica temporal de la información digital relacionada con el hantavirus como caso de un riesgo emergente de salud pública, identificando los principales patrones de actividad y los acontecimientos asociados con incrementos en la atención informativa. Específicamente, se buscó describir las características generales del corpus recuperado, analizar la evolución temporal del volumen de publicaciones e identificar los principales periodos de incremento de actividad informativa y los acontecimientos predominantes asociados con ellos. pág. 5866 METODOLOGÍA Diseño del estudio Se realizó un estudio observacional, retrospectivo, descriptivo y exploratorio para analizar la dinámica temporal de publicaciones digitales en español relacionadas con el hantavirus. La unidad de análisis fue cada publicación incluida en el corpus y la actividad informativa se determinó a partir de su frecuencia de publicación. El periodo analizado comprendió del 7 de mayo al 8 de agosto de 2026. Construcción y depuración del corpus Las publicaciones fueron recuperadas mediante un proceso automatizado de monitoreo de fuentes digitales relacionadas con hantavirus. De 1,693 registros recuperados, se seleccionaron 1,054 publicaciones en español correspondientes al canal de monitoreo orientado a México. Posteriormente, se excluyeron 146 publicaciones anteriores al 7 de mayo de 2026 y nueve registros sin fecha de publicación válida, obteniéndose un corpus final de 899 publicaciones para el periodo del 7 de mayo al 8 de agosto de 2026. La Figura 1 resume el proceso de selección y delimitación del corpus. La orientación del canal hacia México corresponde al criterio de recuperación y no implica que todos los acontecimientos reportados hayan ocurrido en territorio mexicano. Preparación de los datos y construcción de la serie temporal Se utilizaron la fecha de publicación, título, fuente, URL y contenido textual disponible. La fecha de publicación se estableció como referencia temporal y los registros se agruparon por día para construir una serie de frecuencia diaria. Los días sin registros en el corpus se asignaron con frecuencia cero, indicando ausencia de publicaciones recuperadas para esa fecha y no ausencia de información en el conjunto de medios digitales. pág. 5867 Figura 1. Proceso de selección y delimitación del corpus Análisis descriptivo e identificación de episodios de alta actividad Se calcularon estadísticos descriptivos de la frecuencia diaria de publicaciones, incluyendo media, mediana, desviación estándar y valor máximo. Para identificar los días de alta actividad informativa se utilizó un criterio exploratorio basado en la distribución de la frecuencia diaria. Siguiendo un enfoque de umbralización basado en la media y la desviación estándar utilizado previamente para identificar incrementos de actividad en series temporales de información digital (Mantzaris, 2014), se estableció como umbral operacional la suma de la media diaria y una desviación estándar, de acuerdo con la siguiente expresión: U= x̅ + s donde U representa el umbral de alta actividad informativa, x̅ corresponde a la media del número de publicaciones por día y s a la desviación estándar de la frecuencia diaria. En el corpus analizado, la media fue de 9.56 publicaciones por día y la desviación estándar de 28.30, por lo que el umbral obtenido fue: U= 9.56 + 28.30 = 37.86 En consecuencia, se consideraron días de alta actividad aquellos con una frecuencia superior a 37.86 publicaciones, equivalente en términos prácticos a 38 o más publicaciones en un día. Este procedimiento pág. 5868 permitió identificar los días cuya frecuencia de publicaciones fue superior al umbral operacional definido para el estudio. Los días de alta actividad identificados se agruparon posteriormente en episodios. Los días de alta actividad separados por no más de un día intermedio se agruparon en un mismo episodio. Una separación mayor marcó el inicio de un nuevo episodio. Para cada uno se registró como fecha pico aquella con la mayor frecuencia de publicaciones. El umbral y el criterio de agrupación tuvieron un propósito exploratorio y descriptivo, orientado a caracterizar concentraciones temporales de la actividad informativa. No se utilizaron como pruebas de significancia estadística ni como indicadores de cambios epidemiológicos. Caracterización de los principales episodios informativos Para caracterizar los principales episodios, se revisaron los títulos únicos correspondientes a la fecha de máxima actividad de cada uno. La clasificación se realizó manualmente y consideró únicamente la información explícita en el título. Se definieron ocho categorías: caso confirmado o sospechoso, brote o incremento de casos, fallecimiento asociado, alerta o advertencia sanitaria, vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica, prevención y recomendaciones, respuesta o información institucional, y otro o información general. Cuando un mismo título apareció en varios registros, se conservó su frecuencia de aparición. Este valor se utilizó para estimar el peso relativo de cada categoría en la fecha pico. Análisis de sensibilidad Se realizó un análisis de sensibilidad mediante una segunda serie temporal con una sola observación por URL, comparándola con la serie completa. El análisis principal conservó todos los registros, considerando que la repetición de contenidos puede reflejar la intensidad de circulación de la información digital. La serie con URL únicas permitió verificar la estabilidad de los principales patrones temporales al reducir el efecto de contenidos repetidos. RESULTADOS Características generales del corpus El corpus final estuvo integrado por 899 publicaciones, correspondientes a 787 títulos y 811 URL únicas, distribuidas en 94 días calendario. La frecuencia media fue de 9.56 publicaciones por día (DE = 28.30), con una mediana de 1 publicación diaria y un máximo de 169 publicaciones. pág. 5869 Tabla 1. Características generales del corpus analizado Indicador Valor Publicaciones analizadas 899 Títulos únicos 787 URL únicas 811 Periodo de observación 94 días Media diaria 9.56 Mediana diaria 1 Desviación estándar 28.30 Máximo diario 169 Dinámica temporal y episodios de alta actividad Se identificaron seis días de alta actividad informativa, agrupados en tres episodios (P1–P3) (Figura 2; Tabla 2). Sus máximos se registraron el 7, 12 y 19 de mayo, con 78, 139 y 169 publicaciones, respectivamente. En conjunto, los seis días concentraron 643 publicaciones (71.5% del corpus). Figura 2. Dinámica temporal de las publicaciones digitales en español relacionadas con hantavirus. La línea discontinua representa el umbral de alta actividad (media + 1 DE = 37.9 publicaciones/día); P1– P3 indican los episodios identificados. La composición informativa mostró diferencias entre los tres episodios. P1 presentó el perfil más heterogéneo y ninguna categoría alcanzó un predominio claro. La información general reunió la mayor proporción de publicaciones (33.3%), seguida por los contenidos sobre casos confirmados o pág. 5870 sospechosos (21.8%) y la respuesta o información institucional (16.7%). En P2, la respuesta o información institucional adquirió mayor presencia (46.8%), mientras que las alertas o advertencias sanitarias representaron el 21.6%. Ambas categorías concentraron el 68.3% de las publicaciones registradas en la fecha pico. P3 mostró un patrón diferente, dominado por contenidos de vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica (41.4%). La información general representó el 24.3% y las alertas o advertencias sanitarias el 20.1%. Las tres categorías reunieron el 85.8% de las publicaciones de la fecha de máxima actividad. Tabla 2. Episodios de alta actividad informativa y acontecimientos predominantes Episodio Periodo Fecha pico Máximo diario Publicaciones* Acontecimiento predominante** P1 7–8 mayo 7 mayo 78 141 Otro / información general (33.3%) P2 12–14 mayo 12 mayo 139 333 Respuesta o información institucional (46.8%) P3 19 mayo 19 mayo 169 169 Vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica (41.4%) * Publicaciones correspondientes a los días de alta actividad que integraron cada episodio. ** Categoría predominante en la fecha pico, ponderada por la frecuencia de aparición de los títulos. Análisis de sensibilidad El análisis con URL únicas mantuvo los tres máximos temporales (Figura 3). Los valores de las fechas pico pasaron de 78 a 74 en P1, de 139 a 118 en P2 y de 169 a 152 en P3, mostrando que los episodios identificados persistieron al reducir el efecto de contenidos repetidos. Figura 3. Análisis de sensibilidad de la dinámica temporal considerando la serie completa y las URL únicas. pág. 5871 DISCUSIÓN La información digital relacionada con hantavirus mostró una marcada concentración temporal y diferencias en la composición de los episodios identificados. P1 presentó un perfil heterogéneo, mientras que en P2 tuvo mayor presencia la información institucional y en P3 los contenidos de vigilancia o investigación epidemiológica. Este comportamiento coincide con estudios que han documentado variaciones en la atención y en el contenido de la cobertura mediática durante brotes y emergencias sanitarias. El volumen y los temas abordados pueden cambiar conforme determinados acontecimientos adquieren interés público (Kim, 2022; Gozzi et al., 2020; Tizzoni et al., 2020; Wirz et al., 2022; Islam et al., 2023). Los incrementos observados representan cambios en la actividad informativa y no en la intensidad epidemiológica. La atención generada en medios y otras fuentes digitales puede seguir una dinámica distinta a la evolución de los casos o del riesgo sanitario (Tizzoni et al., 2020; Gozzi et al., 2020; Sousa- Pinto et al., 2020). El seguimiento de estas variaciones ofrece información complementaria para caracterizar el entorno informativo asociado con acontecimientos de salud pública. También puede contribuir a la vigilancia situacional y a la comunicación de riesgos, como parte de enfoques que incorporan fuentes y sistemas de información adicionales a los mecanismos tradicionales de vigilancia (Mavragani, 2020; Berg et al., 2021; McClymont et al., 2024; Barrientos-Gutiérrez et al., 2025). El alcance de estos resultados está condicionado por las fuentes disponibles y por el proceso de recuperación, cuya continuidad presentó interrupciones durante el periodo analizado. Los patrones descritos corresponden exclusivamente al corpus recuperado y no representan una medición exhaustiva de la cobertura digital sobre hantavirus. Estudios posteriores podrían incorporar periodos continuos de observación, una mayor diversidad de fuentes y otros riesgos sanitarios para determinar si estos patrones se reproducen en diferentes contextos de salud pública. CONCLUSIONES En este estudio se caracterizó la dinámica temporal de publicaciones digitales en español relacionadas con hantavirus como caso de un riesgo emergente de salud pública. analysis.background: The article examines the temporal dynamics of Spanish‑language digital information about hantavirus as an example of an emerging public‑health risk (A1).
analysis.methods: An observational, retrospective, descriptive and exploratory study used digital publications retrieved through a monitoring channel focused on Mexico (A2); of 1,054 retrieved items, 899 formed the final corpus covering 7 May–8 Aug 2026 (A3); selection excluded records without a valid date (A4).
analysis.results: Three main activity episodes showed peak daily counts of 78, 139 and 169 publications (A6); six high‑activity days accounted for 71.5 % of the corpus (A7); the highest volume occurred on 19 May, when 41.4 % of items related to epidemiological surveillance or investigation (A8); overall information activity was temporally concentrated and varied in composition across episodes (A9).
analysis.contribution: These patterns characterize how the information environment evolved in response to public‑health events, providing insight for infodemiology and risk‑communication monitoring (A10).

papers.title: Ecological and Individual-Level Factors Associated With Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome Notifications and in-Hospital Mortality Among Hospitalized Patients in Chile, 2005-2022.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) is a severe zoonotic disease caused by Orthohantavirus andesense (Andes virus, ANDV), with significant public health burden in Chile. Despite decades of surveillance, knowledge gaps remain regarding the ecological drivers of notification burden and the individual-level determinants of in-hospital mortality among hospitalized patients. This study aimed to address both dimensions simultaneously, providing a multilevel characterization of HCPS epidemiology in Chile from 2005 to 2022. METHODS: Two complementary analyses were conducted. First, an ecological study examined district-level HCPS notifications (2005-2022) using a negative binomial mixed-effects model, with predictors including male population rate, urbanization proportion, population density, season and burned area due to forest fires during the most recent summer season. Second, an individual-level analysis of hospitalized HCPS patients (2010-2020) used a logistic mixed-effects model to identify correlates of in-hospital mortality among hospitalized patients, including age, sex, indigenous group affiliation, hospitalization duration and number of surgical interventions. RESULTS: A total of 886 HCPS cases were notified across 187 districts, averaging 49.2 cases per year. Notifications were positively associated with higher male population rates and greater burned area due to forest fires, and negatively associated with urbanization and population density. Among 462 hospitalized patients, the in-hospital case-fatality ratio was 19.7%. Older age, female sex and indigenous group affiliation were significantly associated with higher in-hospital mortality risk among hospitalized patients. Shorter hospitalization duration and greater number of surgical interventions, as correlates of clinical severity and complexity, were also associated with in-hospital mortality among hospitalized patients. CONCLUSIONS: HCPS notification burden in Chile is shaped by environmental and demographic factors, with forest fire activity representing a novel and actionable ecological risk indicator. In-hospital mortality among hospitalized patients is disproportionately concentrated in older, female, and indigenous populations, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance, equitable healthcare access and integrated One Health strategies to reduce the burden of HCPS in Chile.

papers.title_zh: 2005-2022年智利住院患者的汉坦病毒心肺综合征通报及院内死亡率的生态学与个体层面因素关联

analysis_zh.background: 由安第斯病毒引起的汉坦病毒心肺综合征是一种在智利造成重大公共卫生负担的严重人畜共患疾病 (A1)。关于通报负担的生态驱动因素以及院内死亡率的个体决定因素仍存在知识空白 (A2)。
analysis_zh.methods: 进行两项互补分析:1 基于地区层面通报数据(2005‐2022)的生态负二项混合效应模型,变量包括男性人口比例、城市化程度、人口密度、季节和燃烧面积 (A5);2 基于住院患者(2010‐2020)的个体层面逻辑混合效应模型,评估年龄、性别、土著身份、住院时长及外科手术次数 (A6)。
analysis_zh.results: 共在187个地区通报886例汉坦病毒心肺综合征病例(年均49.2例) (A7)。通报数量随男性人口比例和燃烧面积增加而上升,随城市化程度和人口密度提高而下降 (A8)。462名住院患者中,院内致死率为19.7% (A9)。死亡率较高与年龄较大、女性、土著身份、住院时间较短以及外科手术次数较多相关 (A10‐A11)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究将森林火灾活动确定为汉坦病毒心肺综合征负担的创新生态风险指示器,并显示年龄较大、女性和土著患者的院内死亡率更高,为智利的精准监测和One Health策略提供依据 (A12‐A13)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要;未报告详细方法、样本量依据及潜在混杂因素等信息。

papers.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in children: a systematic scoping review of presentation, critical care management, and outcomes.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome/hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HCPS/HPS) is rare but can progress rapidly from a nonspecific febrile prodrome to respiratory failure, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction. Pediatric-specific evidence is limited, and a comprehensive map of the clinical literature is lacking. METHODS: We conducted a systematic scoping review per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidance (protocol registered at DOI:10.17605/OSF.IO/MZDN4). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to May 2026. Eligible reports described children or adolescents (age ≤18 years) with HCPS/HPS and extractable pediatric clinical data. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed overlap, extracted data, and appraised reporting quality using Joanna Briggs Institute tools. analysis.background: Pediatric hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS/HPS) is rare but can evolve quickly from a nonspecific febrile prodrome to respiratory failure, shock, and multiorgan dysfunction (A1).
analysis.main_directions: The review highlights the paucity of pediatric‑specific evidence and aims to map clinical presentation, critical‑care interventions (mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support, ECMO, renal replacement) and outcomes (A2, A9, A10).
analysis.current_state: From 2,208 records, 20 reports (mainly case‑based from the Americas) were synthesized, showing common features such as fever, GI symptoms, thrombocytopenia, pulmonary edema and a mortality of ~33‑37% (A7, A8, A11, A12).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Pediatric HCPS/HPS is rare but can progress rapidly to severe organ failure (A1). Future research: Prospective registries, standardized reporting, and outcome studies of advanced support are needed (A13, A14).

papers.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: challenges faced by clinicians.

source_records.title: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome: challenges faced by clinicians.

papers.full_text: Managing hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) in pediatric patients is highly challenging due to rapid clinical decline, diagnostic ambiguity, and the lack of targeted antiviral therapies. The article by Weerapong et al addresses these challenges in this issue of Baylor University Medical Center Proceedings.1 While the disease is rare in children, it carries a very high mortality rate of 30% to 50% if not managed aggressively. Because children possess unique physiological vulnerabilities, clinicians face several distinct obstacles when managing HCPS. Diagnostic dilemmas and misinterpretations stem from the nonspecific prodrome, which consists of flu-like symptoms including fever, headache, myalgia, and gastrointestinal issues such as vomiting or abdominal pain. These symptoms mirror common, benign childhood infections like influenza, gastroenteritis, or respiratory syncytial virus, thereby delaying clinical suspicion. Furthermore, obtaining a clear history of rodent exposure is difficult, as children may not notice or recall contact with deer mouse droppings while playing outdoors. Crucially, the shift from a benign viral prodrome to severe respiratory failure and cardiogenic shock occurs abruptly, often within hours. Diffuse pulmonary capillary leakage causes massive, bilateral pleural effusions and pulmonary edema. Unlike typical septic shock, HCPS causes profound myocardial depression marked by an abnormally low cardiac index and elevated systemic vascular resistance. The lack of targeted drug therapies restricts clinical options purely to supportive care. Aggressive fluid resuscitation to correct hypotension routinely worsens pulmonary edema and hypoxemia due to the underlying capillary leak. Consequently, managing low cardiac output requires early, carefully titrated inotropic therapy rather than massive volume expansion. Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation serves as the primary rescue therapy for refractory shock, but its deployment requires specialized pediatric centers and carries significant risks of severe hemorrhage or limb ischemia. Ultimately, successful management hinges on maintaining a high index of suspicion when history suggests exposure, initiating early and aggressive treatment for shock and respiratory failure, and ensuring rapid transfer to high-acuity pediatric centers. — Jamil A. Abbasi, MD Baylor Scott & White All Saints Medical Center, Fort Worth, Texas, USA jamil.abbasi@bswhealth.org References - 1.Lilitwat W, Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, et al. Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in children: a systematic scoping review of presentation, critical care management, and outcomes. Proc (Bayl Univ Med Cent). 2026;39(6):1118–1127. doi: 10.1080/08998280.2026.2698359. [DOI] [PubMed] [Google Scholar]

papers.title: Rabies, Coronavirus, and Hantavirus Surveillance in Bats From the Atlantic Forest of Northeastern Argentina.
papers.abstract: Bats are increasingly recognized as reservoirs of numerous emerging and re-emerging zoonotic pathogens. However, little is known about the distribution of most hosts and viruses and the role of each bat species in transmission, particularly in South America. This study screened for orthohantavirus, rabies, and coronavirus infection, and characterized bat communities from Misiones Province, Argentina, during 2022-2025. At least 14 bat species were captured 1214 times. Blood samples were tested for orthohantavirus-specific antibodies by ELISA. Buccopharyngeal swabs were screened by two separate real-time RT-PCR assays: a pan-lyssavirus assay and a pan-coronavirus assay. Lyssavirus rabies RNA was detected in two individuals (Sturnira lilium and Artibeus lituratus), representing the first confirmed record in S. lilium in Argentina. Coronavirus RNA was detected in two Sturnira lilium, one Carollia perspicillata, and one Artibeus lituratus. Two of these samples, corresponding to C. perspicillata and A. lituratus, were successfully characterized as Alphacoronavirus. No antibodies against orthohantavirus were detected. These findings confirm high bat diversity and viral circulation in frugivorous bats, supporting integrated surveillance.

papers.title_zh: 狂犬病、冠状病毒及汉坦病毒在阿根廷东北大西洋森林蝙蝠中的监测

analysis_zh.background: 蝙蝠日益被认定为众多新发和再发人畜共患病原的储存宿主,但南美洲大多数宿主和病毒的分布尚不清楚。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究于2022‐2025年在阿根廷米西奥内斯省筛查蝙蝠群落,捕获至少14个物种,共计1,214次;血液样本通过ELISA检测正汉坦病毒抗体,口咽拭子使用泛狂犬病毒和泛冠状病毒实时RT‐PCR检测。
analysis_zh.results: 在两只蝙蝠(Sturnira lilium 和 Artibeus lituratus)中检测到狂犬病毒RNA;在四只蝙蝠(两只S. lilium、一只Carollia perspicillata、一只A. lituratus)中检测到冠状病毒RNA,其中两份样本被鉴定为α冠状病毒;未检测到正汉坦病毒抗体。
analysis_zh.contribution: 这些发现证实了果食蝙蝠的高多样性和活跃的病毒循环,支持在大西洋森林地区开展综合监测的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations: 仅提供摘要,限制了对方法、样本量和统计分析细节的了解。

papers.title: Prevalence and Genetic Diversity of Zoonotic Leptospira and Hantavirus in Rodents, Lanxi City, 2023-2025.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis (caused by Leptospira, a bacterium) and hantavirus disease (caused by hantavirus, a virus) are important zoonoses with rodents as main reservoirs. In this study, we investigated the prevalence and genetic diversity of Leptospira and hantavirus in rodents from rural Lanxi City, Zhejiang Province. Rodents showed a higher Leptospira carriage rate than the national average. All hantavirus isolates were Seoul virus (SEOV) and displayed high genetic divergence from vaccine strains. Notably, a unique local phylogenetic cluster of Leptospira borgpetersenii was identified, indicating potential vaccine mismatch and local evolutionary divergence. METHODS: Samples were collected from April 2023 to August 2025, with intensive trapping from April to August annually in 2023-2024 and additional sampling in April 2025. Liver and kidney tissues were collected via aseptic dissection. Real-time fluorescent PCR was used to detect pathogen nucleic acids, and gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis were performed on positive samples. RESULTS: A total of 350 rodents were captured, with Rattus norvegicus (brown rat) as the dominant species (80.00%). The overall Leptospira carriage rate was 7.14% (25/350), with the highest rate in R. norvegicus (7.86%). The overall hantavirus carriage rate was 1.43% (5/350), distributed mainly in R. norvegicus and Rattus flavipectus (yellow-breasted rat). No coinfection with both pathogens was detected. Genetic analysis identified 12 Leptospira strains as Leptospira interrogans and 2 as L. borgpetersenii; the latter showed genetic differences from domestic and foreign strains, suggesting a potential evolutionary trend. The two hantavirus strains were both SEOV, closely related to domestic SEOV strains from 2021 but with only 86.08-86.81% nucleotide homology to vaccine strains (e.g., 80-39, Z37), indicating natural variation. CONCLUSIONS: Rodents in rural Lanxi have a relatively high Leptospira carriage rate, and hantavirus is dominated by the SEOV type. R. norvegicus is the main host of both pathogens. Targeted monitoring and prevention/control measures should be strengthened. Natural genetic variation suggests potential antigenic drift and reduced vaccine matching, which requires further serological validation. Attention should be paid to the impact of pathogen genetic variation on control efforts.
papers.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)

papers.title_zh: 2023-2025年兰溪市啮齿动物中人畜共患性钩端螺旋体及汉坦病毒的流行率与遗传多样性

analysis_zh.background: 钩端螺旋体病和 汉坦病毒 是以啮齿动物为主要宿主的人畜共患疾病。
analysis_zh.methods: 2023年4月至2025年8月在浙江省兰溪市农村捕获啮齿动物;无菌采集其肝、肾组织,采用实时荧光PCR检测,随后进行基因测序和系统发育分析。

papers.title: The 2026 Andes hantavirus outbreak: a renewed call for global zoonotic preparedness
papers.abstract: The 2026 cluster of Andes virus (ANDV) infection linked to the expedition cruise ship MV Hondius resulted in 13 cases (12 laboratory-confirmed and one probable), including three deaths, and required the monitoring of more than 650 contacts across more than 30 countries and territories before the World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak over on 2 July 2026. Available evidence suggests a single land-based zoonotic exposure before embarkation, followed by limited person-to-person transmission on board. Although WHO assessed the global risk as low throughout, the event exposed recurring weaknesses in zoonotic preparedness, including delayed clinical recognition in a remote setting, maritime outbreak protocols oriented toward other pathogens, and the burden of multinational contact tracing for an infection with an incubation period of up to 6 weeks. This editorial examines these lessons in light of earlier ANDV outbreaks and argues for closer integration of One Health surveillance, maritime health security, and the International Health Regulations in preparing for rare but high-consequence zoonoses.
papers.journal: International Journal of Surgery: Global Health

papers.title: Ecological Correlates and Spatiotemporal Trends of Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome in West Kazakhstan: A 25-Year One Health Surveillance Study (2001–2025)
papers.abstract: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a rodent-borne zoonosis of public health concern in West Kazakhstan, yet long-term studies linking human and reservoir surveillance are scarce. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HFRS cases (2001–2025) and routine rodent surveillance data from five districts of the West Kazakhstan Region within a One Health framework. Associations were estimated using negative binomial regression with district fixed effects and year-clustered robust standard errors (2002–2024; 115 district-years). Overall, 314 cases were recorded (81.2% male), with a major outbreak in 2005 (85 cases) and a resurgence in 2024–2025 (27 and 41 cases). Burlinsky District reported the most cases (44.9%), whereas Baiterek District had the highest incidence in 2016–2025. Of 132,694 rodents examined, 1083 (0.82%) were hantavirus antigen-positive. A larger share of the annual Mus musculus catch obtained in spring–summer was associated with higher case counts (incidence rate ratio 1.051 per percentage point; 95% CI: 1.024–1.080), and this was robust to excluding outbreak years. The number of positive rodents was associated with cases, but not after standardization for sampling effort. These associations do not establish M. musculus as a reservoir and are consistent with, but do not demonstrate, increased peridomestic exposure.

analysis.background: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a rodent‑borne zoonosis of public‑health concern in West Kazakhstan, but long‑term integrated human‑reservoir studies are scarce (A1).
analysis.methods: Laboratory‑confirmed HFRS cases (2001‑2025) and routine rodent surveillance from five districts were analyzed within a One Health framework; associations were estimated using negative‑binomial regression with district fixed effects and year‑clustered robust standard errors (2002‑2024, 115 district‑years) (A2, A3, A4).
analysis.results: Overall 314 cases (81.2 % male) were recorded, with peaks in 2005 (85 cases) and 2024‑2025 (27 and 41 cases); Burlinsky District contributed 44.9 % of cases and Baiterek had the highest recent incidence (A5, A6). Of 132,694 rodents examined, 1083 (0.82 %) were hantavirus antigen‑positive (A7). A larger spring‑summer share of Mus musculus captures was associated with higher case counts (IRR 1.051 per percentage point; 95 % CI 1.024‑1.080), robust to exclusion of outbreak years (A8, A9); the number of positive rodents correlated with cases only before standardizing for sampling effort (A10).
analysis.contribution: The study provides a 25‑year One Health surveillance dataset linking human HFRS incidence with rodent ecological variables, identifying potential environmental drivers for public‑health monitoring (A2, A8).
analysis.limitations: The reported associations do not establish Mus musculus as a reservoir nor demonstrate increased peridomestic exposure, and only abstract information is available (A11, A12).

analysis.summary_en: Background: HFRS is a rodent‑borne zoonosis of concern in West Kazakhstan, yet long‑term integrated studies are scarce (A1). Methods: Confirmed cases (2001‑2025) and rodent surveillance from five districts were analyzed in a One Health framework using negative‑binomial regression with district fixed effects and year‑clustered robust SEs (2002‑2024, 115 district‑years) (A2‑A4). Results: 314 cases (81.2 % male) peaked in 2005 and 2024‑2025; Burlinsky contributed 44.9 % of cases, Baiterek had highest recent incidence; 0.82 % of 132,694 rodents were hantavirus‑positive; higher spring‑summer Mus musculus capture share linked to higher case counts (IRR 1.051 per % point; 95 % CI 1.024‑1.080) and rodent positivity correlated with cases only before effort standardization (A5‑A10). Contribution: Provides a 25‑year One Health dataset linking human HFRS with rodent ecology, identifying environmental drivers for surveillance (A2, A8). Limitations: Associations do not prove Mus musculus as a reservoir nor increased peridomestic exposure, and only abstract data are available (A11, A12).

papers.title_zh: 西哈萨克斯坦 肾综合征出血热 的生态相关因素与时空趋势:一项跨越25年的一体化健康监测研究(2001–2025)

analysis_zh.background: 肾综合征出血热(HFRS)是西哈萨克斯坦一种由啮齿动物传播的公共卫生关注的动物源性疾病,但长期的综合人类‐宿主研究稀缺(A1)。
analysis_zh.methods: 对五个地区的实验室确诊 HFRS 病例(2001‐2025)和常规啮齿动物监测数据在一体化健康框架下进行分析;关联性采用负二项回归估计,加入地区固定效应和按年份聚类的稳健标准误(2002‐2024,115 个地区‐年)(A2、A3、A4)。
analysis_zh.contribution: 本研究提供了跨越 25 年的一体化健康监测数据集,将人类 HFRS 发病率与啮齿动物生态变量关联,识别出潜在的环境驱动因素,可用于公共卫生监测(A2、A8)。
analysis_zh.limitations: 报告的关联并未证明 Mus musculus 为宿主,也未显示居家周边暴露增加,且仅有摘要信息可得(A11、A12)。

papers.title: Đặc điểm dịch tễ học các ca nhiễm Hantavirus ở người và tình trạng nhiễm trên chuột tại địa điểm có ca bệnh, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh, 2012 – 2014: Báo cáo loạt ca
papers.abstract: Nghiên cứu hồi cứu này nhằm mô tả đặc điểm dịch tễ các trường hợp nhiễm Hantavirus ở người và xácđịnh tỷ lệ mẫu huyết thanh chuột dương tính với Hantavirus tại các địa điểm ghi nhận ca bệnh ở Thànhphố Hồ Chí Minh giai đoạn 2012–2014. Dữ liệu được thu thập từ hệ thống giám sát bệnh truyền nhiễm củaViện Pasteur Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh. Kết quả ghi nhận 6 ca nhiễm Hantavirus ở người, không có tử vong.Năm 2014 có số ca cao nhất với 3 ca (50,0%); nam giới chiếm 83,3% và phần lớn ca bệnh trên 30 tuổi.Tất cả đều tăng creatinine huyết thanh (173–671 μmol/L), trong đó 4 ca giảm tiểu cầu (11.000–58.000 tếbào/mm3); tất cả đều hồi phục sau điều trị. Chuột và chất thải chuột được ghi nhận tại nơi sinh sống của tấtcả bệnh nhân. Trong 309 mẫu huyết thanh chuột được xét nghiệm, có 88 mẫu dương tính với Hantavirus(28,5%); tỷ trọng mẫu dương tính cao nhất được ghi nhận ở chuột cống (Rattus norvegicus) (87,5%). Kếtquả cho thấy Hantavirus lưu hành trong quần thể chuột tại các địa điểm ghi nhận ca bệnh, tiềm ẩn nguycơ phơi nhiễm ở người trong môi trường đô thị. Cần tăng cường giám sát ca bệnh, năng lực xét nghiệmHantavirus và giám sát định kỳ trên chuột nhằm hỗ trợ phát hiện sớm và triển khai các biện pháp phòng,chống kịp thời.
papers.journal: Tạp chí Y học Dự phòng

analysis.background: The study aimed to describe the epidemiological characteristics of human hantavirus infections and determine the seroprevalence of hantavirus in rodent samples at sites with reported cases in Ho Chi Minh City (2012‑2014).
analysis.methods: Retrospective analysis of data from the Pasteur Institute’s infectious disease surveillance system; human case data and rodent serum samples were collected from sites with reported cases.
analysis.results: Six human hantavirus cases were recorded (no deaths); 2014 had the highest number (3 cases, 50.0%). 83.3% were male, most were over 30 years. All cases had elevated serum creatinine (173–671 µmol/L) and 4 had thrombocytopenia (11,000–58,000 cells/mm³). All recovered. Of 309 rodent serum samples, 88 (28.5%) were hantavirus‑positive; the highest positivity (87.5%) was in sewer rats (Rattus norvegicus).

analysis.limitations: Only abstract data are available; detailed methods, sample characteristics, and causality are not reported. The small number of human cases limits generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The study aimed to describe the epidemiology of human hantavirus infections and determine rodent seroprevalence in Ho Chi Minh City (2012‑2014). Methods: Retrospective analysis of surveillance data from the Pasteur Institute, including human cases and rodent serum samples. papers.title: Hantaviruses at the human-animal-environment interface: a One Health review of rodent reservoirs, surveillance, and preparedness
papers.abstract: Hantaviruses maintained in small mammals cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome. Exposure usually arises from contact with infected rodent excreta, so prevention depends on understanding reservoir ecology, human activities, and the settings in which they intersect. This structured narrative review synthesizes evidence on host relationships, exposure, clinical and laboratory recognition, genomic investigation, and One Health surveillance across several regions. We propose three risk-proportionate tiers: baseline readiness where evidence is sparse, enhanced investigation after a credible signal, and sustained integrated surveillance where transmission is established. Five shared functions are scaled across tiers: reservoir sampling, clinical recognition and referral testing, molecular characterization, occupational and environmental assessment, and cross-sector data review. Published outbreaks in Croatia and long-running surveillance in Panama illustrate how the decision logic could be applied, while the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship event highlights the need for diagnostics and contact management. The framework provides a practical way to plan surveillance with limited resources, but its triggers, workload, and impact remain to be evaluated prospectively.

papers.title: Continent-wide Multi-Segment Phylogenomic Study of Host and Geographic Structuring of African Hantaviruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: African hantaviruses remain among the least characterized members of the family Hantaviridae , with fragmented genomic data limiting our understanding of their evolutionary relationships, host associations, and geographic structuring. Here, we investigated the integrated continent-wide phylogenomic structure of African hantaviruses using all three coding genomic segments. Methods: We compiled and curated 281 full-length and partial coding sequences representing the L segment ( n = 166), M segment ( n = 48), and S segment ( n = 67) from 13 African countries, alongside representative global reference strains. Temporal signal was evaluated using root-to-tip regression analysis. Segment-specific phylogenetic reconstructions were performed to characterize host-associated and geographic structuring. Additionally, pairwise tanglegram comparisons of the L, M, and S phylogenies were constructed to evaluate topological congruence and identify potential signals of genetic reassortment. Results Root-to-tip regressions revealed weak temporal signal across the L ( R 2 = 0.069), M ( R 2 = 0.021), and S ( R 2 = 0.046) datasets, precluding reliable molecular-clock inference. Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated pronounced host-associated and geographic structuring across all three segments. Rodent, shrew, and bat-associated hantaviruses formed distinct evolutionary clades, with bat and shrew-borne lineages occupying basal, divergent positions relative to rodent-associated viruses. Endemic African hantaviruses exhibited marked regional clustering, forming distinct Malagasy, East African, and West African assemblages, whereas Senegalese, Beninese, and Malian sequences clustered within globally distributed, Rattus -associated Seoul orthohantavirus lineages. Comparative analyses highlighted complementary phylogenetic signals: the L segment provided a robust framework for resolving deep evolutionary relationships, the M segment offered clear discrimination among closely related host and geographic groups, and the S segment consistently recovered primary lineage boundaries. Pairwise tanglegrams demonstrated substantial topological concordance among segments highest between L and M with localized incongruences primarily in the L–S comparison restricted to closely related terminal taxa, consistent with but not definitive evidence of reassortment Conclusions African hantaviruses display strong host-associated and geographic structuring, with major evolutionary relationships broadly conserved across all three genomic segments. These findings provide an integrated continent-wide phylogenomic framework, establishing a foundation for future genomic surveillance, evolutionary studies, and One Health strategies across Africa.

analysis.background: African hantaviruses are among the least characterized hantavirids, with fragmented genomic data limiting understanding of their evolution, host links, and geographic patterns.
analysis.methods: The study compiled 281 full‑length and partial coding sequences (L n=166, M n=48, S n=67) from 13 African countries and global references, evaluated temporal signal via root‑to‑tip regression, performed segment‑specific phylogenetic reconstructions, and used pairwise tanglegram comparisons to assess topological concordance and possible reassortment.
analysis.results: Root‑to‑tip regressions showed weak temporal signal (L R²=0.069, M R²=0.021, S R²=0.046), precluding reliable molecular‑clock dating; phylogenies revealed strong host‑associated and geographic structuring, with distinct rodent, shrew, and bat clades and regional clusters (Malagasy, East African, West African) plus some sequences embedded in globally distributed Seoul virus lineages; segment analyses provided complementary resolution, and tanglegrams indicated high concordance, especially between L and M, with limited incongruence suggesting possible reassortment.
analysis.contribution: The work delivers an integrated continent‑wide phylogenomic framework for African hantaviruses, supporting future genomic surveillance, evolutionary research, and One Health initiatives across Africa.
analysis.limitations: Weak temporal signal limits molecular‑clock inference, and only abstract‑level data are available, restricting detail on methods and broader contextual information.

analysis.summary_en: Background: African hantaviruses are poorly characterized, hindering insight into their evolution and host/ geographic patterns. Methods: Researchers assembled 281 L, M, and S segment sequences from 13 African nations, assessed temporal signal, built segment‑specific phylogenies, and compared topologies with tanglegrams. Results: Temporal signal was weak (L R²=0.069, M R²=0.021, S R²=0.046); phylogenies showed strong host‑ and region‑based clustering, distinct rodent, shrew, bat clades, and regional assemblages, with high segment concordance and limited reassortment evidence. Contribution: Provides a continent‑wide phylogenomic baseline for surveillance and One Health strategies. Limitations: Weak temporal signal restricts clock analyses and only abstract data are available.

analysis_zh.methods: 本研究汇总了来自13个非洲国家及全球参考的281条全长和部分编码序列(L n=166,M n=48,S n=67),通过根到尖回归评估时间信号,进行各片段的系统发育重建,并使用成对缠结图比较评估拓扑一致性及可能的重配。
analysis_zh.results: 根到尖回归显示时间信号较弱(L R2=0.069,M R2=0.021,S R2=0.046),无法进行可靠的分子钟估计;系统发育树揭示出显著的宿主和地理结构,形成了分别对应啮齿动物、鼩鼱和蝙蝠的独立分支以及马达加斯加、东非和西非等地区簇,还出现部分序列嵌入全球分布的首尔病毒谱系;各片段分析提供了互补的分辨率,缠结图显示高度一致,尤其是L与M之间,只有少量不一致提示可能的重配。
analysis_zh.contribution: 该工作提供了面向全非洲的综合系统基因组框架,用于非洲汉坦病毒,为未来的基因组监测、进化研究以及全非洲的One Health倡议提供支持。
analysis_zh.limitations: 时间信号弱限制了分子钟推断,且仅有摘要层面的数据可得,导致方法细节和更广泛背景信息受限。

papers.title: Hantavirus: An Emerging Global Zoonotic Threat—From Molecular Basis to Clinical Management and Public Health Perspectives
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infection is an emerging zoonotic viral disease caused by hantaviruses of the family Hantaviridae, primarily transmitted to humans through exposure to infected rodent urine, feces, saliva, or contaminated aerosols. The disease presents mainly in two clinical forms: Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), prevalent in Asia and Europe, and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS)/Hantavirus Cardiopulmonary Syndrome (HCPS), predominantly reported in the Americas. The historical recognition of hantavirus began during the Korean War (1950–1953), when thousands of soldiers developed Korean hemorrhagic fever. In 1978, Ho-Wang Lee isolated the Hantaan virus from Apodemus agrarius, marking a major scientific breakthrough. Subsequent decades witnessed the identification of multiple hantavirus species, including Seoul, Puumala, Dobrava-Belgrade, Sin Nombre, and Andes viruses, each associated with distinct rodent reservoirs and clinical manifestations. A major epidemiological milestone occurred in 1993 with the outbreak of Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome in the Four Corners region of the United States, leading to the discovery of Sin Nombre virus. Increasing urbanization, climate change, deforestation, and closer human–rodent interactions have contributed to the global emergence of hantavirus infections in the 21st century. Advances in molecular diagnostics, including reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and serological testing, have enhanced disease surveillance and early diagnosis. This review highlights the historical evolution, epidemiology, transmission, and growing public health significance of hantavirus infection worldwide. Keywords: Hantavirus infection; Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS); Hantavirus Pulmonary

papers.title: Predictive Surveillance for Andes Virus Transmission in the Americas.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT. The 2026 Andes virus outbreak linked to the M/V Hondius cruise ship exposed limitations in conventional, case-based surveillance for zoonotic threats with potential person-to-person transmission. In the present opinion and analysis article, the authors argue that predictive surveillance, supported by artificial intelligence, ecological modeling, and the One Health approach, can strengthen preparedness for hantavirus transmission in the Americas. Current evidence suggests that selected models that incorporate epidemiological, climatic, environmental, and rodent-related variables may provide an anticipatory window of 2 to 12 months, depending on context and data inputs. However, implementation requires more than technical capacity. It depends on interoperable multisectoral data, transparent model governance, local validation, sustainable financing, and technology transfer to avoid widening inequities between health systems. Predictive surveillance should complement conventional surveillance by supporting risk communication, rodent monitoring, laboratory preparedness, and targeted public health action in areas where ecological and epidemiological signals converge.
papers.journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
